patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2] mm/mempolicy: recompute automatic interleave weights on memory hotplug

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2] mm/mempolicy: recompute automatic interleave weights on memory hotplug

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance regression caused by outdated automatic interleave weights in the Linux kernel's memory policy module (mm/mempolicy). When nodes gain or lose memory, their weights are not recalculated from their reported bandwidths, leading to an uneven distribution of data and potential overload. The patch introduces a new function, wi_state_refresh(), which recomputes the weights based on the recorded bandwidth whenever a node gains or loses its first/last memory. If allocating new weights fails, it warns once and continues with the next recompute starting from the full bandwidth table.

review_comments.author: Andrew Morton
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Andrew Morton noted that the original patch description mentioned that HMAT and CXL report a node's bandwidth only when it first gains memory, but this logic was not correctly applied in the code changes. Specifically, the wi_state_refresh() function should recompute weights whenever N_MEMORY changes, which is already handled by the hotplug notifier. However, the comment also suggests that the original patch description and the code changes are inconsistent, as the original description implies that the weights should be recomputed on every memory hotplug event.

version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm/mempolicy: use one node set for interleave weights

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a divide error on x86 and panic when memory is being online, caused by torn reads on the nodemask N_MEMORY. It records the nodes visited while summing bandwidth and uses that same set for scaling and reducing weights, ensuring consistent state even if N_MEMORY changes.

review_comments.author: Joshua Hahn
review_comments.summary: Approved the fix and added a Reviewed-by tag, considering it makes sense to use a consistent node set for interleave weights.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Fri, Oct 30, 2026 at 12:12 PM Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net> wrote:
>
> From: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
>
> From: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
>
> Switching weighted interleave back to automatic mode while memory is
> being onlined can cause a kernel divide error on x86, and a panic if
> panic_on_oops is set.
>
> reduce_interleave_weights() scans N_MEMORY three times, but hotplug
> can cause N_MEMORY to change at runtime - and torn reads on that
> nodemask can cause a total sum of zero bandwidth.  A node that
> was hot-unplugged and then hotplugged back can then cause this
> loop to generate a div/0.
>
> Record the nodes visited while summing their bandwidth, then use
> that same set when scaling and reducing the weights.  This gives
> us a consistent state even if N_MEMORY changes.

Makes a lot of sense to me. Thanks for the fix!

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a deadlock issue in the mpt3sas driver where a device is blocked by a DELAY_NOT_RESPONDING event, preventing further scan attempts from proceeding. The patch introduces a delayed work to unblock expired devices after a missing delay period plus an additional 30 seconds. This approach ensures that devices are not stuck waiting for a lock and allows the system to recover from such situations.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/6] NFSD: Add per-export read/write I/O mode settings
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds per-export read/write I/O mode settings to the NFS server. It introduces two new fields, 'read-io' and 'write-io', in the struct svc_export to store these settings. The patch also updates the netlink specification to include an io-mode enum and defines NFSD_IO_BUFFERED/DONTCACHE/DIRECT in terms of it. The new options are only accessible through netlink and are parsed on cache update, with their values reported in nfsd.export/content.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/6] NFSD: Apply per-export I/O modes to READ and WRITE
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the NFSD code to apply per-export I/O modes to READ and WRITE operations. It resolves each export's effective I/O mode by checking explicit settings or using the global io_cache_read/write knob. The patch also removes unnecessary coupling between debugfs knobs, allowing for more flexible configuration of I/O behavior on a per-export basis. Additionally, it updates debugfs comments to match the new behavior and introduces a global 'never splice' override.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/6] NFSD: Document per-export read_io= and write_io= options
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds documentation for two new export options in the NFS server: read_io= and write_io=. These options allow administrators to set the I/O mode for each export independently, overriding global settings. The options accept three values: buffered, dontcache, or direct, with the same meanings as their corresponding debugfs values. The patch also explains how these per-export settings interact with global knobs and are reported in /proc/net/rpc/nfsd.export/content.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 4/6] NFSD: Keep per-export statistics across export cache updates
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where per-export statistics in the NFS server are lost when export cache entries are replaced or removed. To solve this, it introduces a new data structure to store these statistics on a per-net basis, keyed by the export root and client name. This allows statistics to be preserved even after cache updates or restarts. A delayed work item is used to free unused statistics after an hour of inactivity.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 5/6] NFSD: Count the storage reads of each export's READs
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new counter to track the storage reads of each export in NFS, which is essential for determining the optimal I/O mode for an export. The current implementation only reports bytes returned by READ operations, but this does not accurately reflect the actual storage reads. To address this issue, the patch introduces a new io_read_storage counter that captures the difference between the read_bytes charged to the submitting task and the initial value of read_bytes when a READ operation starts. This approach accounts for readahead and metadata reads, making it applicable to various types of reads. The new counter is only visible with CONFIG_TASK_IO_ACCOUNTING enabled.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 6/6] NFSD: Document how to choose an IO mode
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds documentation to help administrators choose the correct IO mode for an NFS export, including when to use buffered, dontcache, or direct IO. It explains why a low server page cache hit rate is normal and lists workload conditions that favor each IO mode. The document also describes existing metrics to measure performance, such as per-export miss ratio and client mountstats byte counters.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series adds new export options to the NFS server (nfsd) for controlling read and write I/O modes on a per-export basis, replacing global debugfs switches. The options are read_io= and write_io=, which can be set to buffered, direct, or dontcache. This change aims to provide more fine-grained control over I/O behavior and eventually move these controls to something more permanent.

review_comments.author: Chuck Lever
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Chuck Lever questioned the need for randomizing clientids, session IDs, and COPY_NOTIFY tokens, citing that if a client or middlebox is interpreting these values, it's behavior not supported by the protocol specification (RFC 8881). He suggested there may be alternative ways to provide operational needs, such as correlating packet captures with server-side events or diffing traces between runs.
review_comments.raw_body:
I'd like to understand the use case better. Can you say concretely what
consumes the contents of these tokens, and what breaks when they are
random?

The protocol mandates that nothing on the client side should care about
the non-sequence ID parts of these cookies. RFC 8881 defines the client
ID as a server-chosen shorthand (Section 2.4), gives the stateid's
"other" field no meaning beyond identifying a set of locks (Section
8.2.2), and declares sessionid4 as an opaque array. The seqid field is
the one part of a stateid that carries client-visible semantics, and
this series leaves that field alone; it is still a monotonically
increasing integer.

So if a client or a middlebox is interpreting these values, that is
behavior the spec does not support, and I'm not inclined to add a knob
to accommodate it. On the other hand, if the need is operational, say
correlating packet captures with server-side events or diffing traces
between runs, there may be a better way to provide that than
predictable tokens.


-- 
Chuck Lever (Come to NFS bake-a-thon! https://nfsv4bat.org)

series_items.subject: [PATCH 3/5] iomap: remove ->iomap_begin()/->iomap_end() legacy path
series_items.patch_summary: This patch removes the legacy ->iomap_begin()/->iomap_end() path in the iomap code, as all in-tree filesystems have implemented the ->iomap_next() method. The changes involve updating the iomap_iter function to use the ->iomap_next() method instead of the legacy path and removing the corresponding flags and functions from the iomap_ops structure. This change simplifies the iomap code and reduces its complexity.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 4/5] iomap: pass iomap_iter_next_fn directly instead of struct iomap_ops
series_items.patch_summary: This patch simplifies the iomap code by removing the struct iomap_ops, which only contained a single function pointer. Instead, the iomap_iter_next_fn is passed directly to the iomap_iter and other entry points. This change is possible because all filesystems now implement ->iomap_next() and have removed the legacy fallback. The patch also renames the ops field in the iomap_iter tracepoint to next for consistency.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 5/5] Documentation: iomap: update docs to reflect iomap_iter_next model
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the iomap documentation to reflect a change in how filesystems interact with the iomap API. Specifically, it removes support for separate ->iomap_begin() and ->iomap_end() callbacks, replacing them with a single iomap_iter_next() callback that finishes the previous mapping (if any) and produces the next one. The patch updates documentation across three files to reflect this change.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series converts various filesystems to use the iomap_iter_next() model, which is a more efficient and flexible way of handling I/O operations. The patches are rebased on top of current mainline and require two new preparatory patches for trivial ->iomap_next() conversions. The conversion affects several filesystems, including nilfs2, fuse, ext4, exfat, and others.

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3 0/3] mm: split underused anonymous mTHP folios

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 1/3] mm/huge_memory: scale thp_underused() to the folio size
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the thp_underused() function to be aware of the size of a folio, rather than assuming it's always PMD-sized. It scales the khugepaged_max_ptes_none threshold proportionally to the number of pages in the folio, ensuring that the same fraction of zero-filled pages is tolerated regardless of folio size. This change will prevent issues when collapsing mTHP orders and splitting folios, as both operations would use the same threshold for a given folio size. The patch makes no functional changes for PMD-sized folios, as their nr_pages value remains HPAGE_PMD_NR.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 2/3] mm/huge_memory: don't queue folios when underused splitting is inactive
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the handling of anonymous PMD-sized folios by skipping their queueing when underused splitting is inactive, which happens at the default khugepaged/max_ptes_none setting. This change reduces unnecessary work and improves performance.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
review_comments.summary: Reviewed the patch and found it to be technically sound. The optimization is a good improvement for performance.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Fri, Oct 23, 2026 at 04:00:05PM -0700, Joanne Koong wrote:
> Every anonymous PMD-sized folio is put on the deferred split queue when
> it is first mapped, so that the shrinker can find it under memory
> pressure and split it if it turns out to be mostly zero-filled.
> 
> With the default khugepaged/max_ptes_none this is wasted work. The
> default is HPAGE_PMD_NR - 1, which tells thp_underused() that any number
> of zero-filled pages is tolerable, which means the shrinker will never
> split any of these folios for being underused. They take the list_lru
> lock at fault time, inflate the object count the shrinker reports, and
> are then walked and dropped when they're first scanned.
> 
> Skip the queueing when khugepaged/max_ptes_none is at its maximum, and
> factor that check out into thp_underused_never() so that
> deferred_split_folio() and thp_underused() share it. Since the default
> is the maximum, out of the box no folio is queued for underused
> splitting at all, PMD-sized ones included. Partially mapped folios are
> still queued as before.
> 
> This also matters for a subsequent patch that adds anonymous mTHP folios
> to the deferred split list, as it keeps systems running the default from
> paying for that on every anonymous fault.
> 
> Please note that the queue has always been best-effort. A folio that was
> queued before khugepaged/max_ptes_none is lowered gets dropped from the
> queue by the first scan that finds it's not underused, so changing the
> sysctl has never retroactively applied to folios that were already
> scanned. Requeueing eligible folios when the sysctl changes will be
> addressed in a separate patch.
> 
> Suggested-by: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>
> Suggested-by: David Hildenbrand <david@kernel.org>
> Signed-off-by: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>

Reviewed-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 3/3] mm: add anonymous mTHP folios to the deferred split list
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds anonymous mTHP folios to the deferred split list, allowing them to be split and reclaimed when under memory pressure. This addresses a problem where fully mapped mTHP folios that are mostly zero-filled were not being split due to their size. The patch introduces a minimum size of 2M for mTHP folios to be considered for splitting, which can be adjusted later if needed. It also maintains backwards compatibility by exempting PMD-sized folios from this minimum size. The change is made in the fault path and khugepaged mTHP collapse path, with minimal overhead on the common order-0 fault path.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that thp_underused_split_page starts counting mTHP splits, but this creates inconsistencies in the split counter as it can be larger than thp_split_page and per-order stats do not distinguish between underused and other splits. The reviewer suggested making thp_underused_split_page PMD-only with a separate per-order counter for underused splits.
review_comments.raw_body:
With this, thp_underused_split_page starts counting mTHP splits.
thp_split_page and thp_deferred_split_page count PMD-sized folios only,
and mTHPs get per-order stats instead. thp_underused_split_page can now
be larger than thp_split_page, and the per-order split counter does not
tell underused splits from the rest.

Should thp_underused_split_page stay PMD-only, with a per-order counter
for underused splits?

This is messy. I am not sure excluding non-PMD splits from the counter
is the right call, but it seems to be the most consistent solution.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses memory regressions caused by 2M THP=always on arm64 by allowing the underused shrinker to handle anonymous mTHP folios. The patches make thp_underused() folio-size-aware, stop queuing folios for underused splitting when khugepaged/max_ptes_none is at its default maximum, and queue anonymous mTHP folios of at least 2M on the deferred split list.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
review_comments.summary: Gave Reviewed-by

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that thp_underused_split_page starts counting mTHP splits, which could lead to inconsistent statistics due to the per-order counter not distinguishing between underused and other splits, and suggested making it PMD-only with a separate counter for underused splits.
review_comments.raw_body:
With this, thp_underused_split_page starts counting mTHP splits.
thp_split_page and thp_deferred_split_page count PMD-sized folios only,
and mTHPs get per-order stats instead. thp_underused_split_page can now
be larger than thp_split_page, and the per-order split counter does not
tell underused splits from the rest.

Should thp_underused_split_page stay PMD-only, with a per-order counter
for underused splits?

This is messy. I am not sure excluding non-PMD splits from the counter
is the right call, but it seems to be the most consistent solution.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

review_comments.author: Joanne Koong (author)
review_comments.summary:
Author addressed Kiryl's concern that the patch does not handle the case where khugepaged/max_ptes_none is set to its default maximum, which would prevent underused mTHP folios from being split. Author explained that this is intentional and that the shrinker would never split them anyway.

Author acknowledged the need to handle thp_split_page and thp_deferred_split_page consistently, agreed to make the change in v4.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Kiryl,

Thanks for taking a look at this patch.

---

This is a great point. Your suggestion makes sense to me, to keep it
consistent with how we handle thp_split_page and
thp_deferred_split_page.
I'll make this change for v4, unless anyone else thinks there is a
cleaner way of accounting this.

Thanks,
Joanne

Re: [PATCH 0/5] iomap: remaining patches for iomap_iter_next conversion
Re: [PATCH 2/3] mm/swap: account synchronous swap reads as memory stall
patches_reviewed.patch_summary: This patch modifies the swap read handling in Linux to account for synchronous swap reads as memory stalls. The change is made by adding a condition to the swap_can_merge function that checks if the working set of the current folio matches the one being merged, preventing unnecessary merging when reading from disk. This approach aims to improve performance and reduce memory stall times.

review_comments.author: Kairui Song
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the proposed change has a trade-off between PSI accuracy and batching performance, but suggested merging the current patch with an additional fix to address the issue for sync devices, which would have limited cost due to their batch size being one folio.
review_comments.raw_body:
We are in a dilemma with this change: if it fires frequently it breaks
batching but improves PSI accuracy.  If it doesn't fire frequently, it
has no negative effect on batching and performance, and it isn't helping
with PSI accuracy either :/

But after a second thought, maybe we can live with it by having both this
posted patch merged as it is and appending your suggested fix: the two
kinds of devices end up differently.

For sync devices the batch is now always one folio, so there is nothing
fancy, everything is accurate.  Readahead batching for them only happens
on the MADV and swapoff walks, so the cost is limited.

For async, the window covers submission.  That cost grows only mildly
with the folios in the bio, block layer and dispatch work, unlike a
synchronous read.  And the previous per folio accounting was not
exact either: in a single threaded task, the throttle or cost of
a non-workingset readahead folio pays is also holding up the workingset
folio's refault, since the task cannot start the next submission until
that one returns.  Same story for delayacct.

And we are missing the completion wait either way: if a fault finds the
folio in the swap cache with its read still in flight, it blocks in
folio_lock_or_retry() in do_swap_page(), which no window covers.

So perhaps we can live with it for now by having your suggested fix
on top of this posted patch? Some comments could be helpful here and
maybe some further improvement is needed.
